questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Good courses, focus on marine biology, field work opportunities, nice weather :)

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Australia is a great destination for a biologist, There are many opportunities for weekend trips not far from Townsville, such as Cairns, Airlie Beach, Crystal Creek etc. However the campus is located 40 min bus ride from the city, making it quite isolated, and a car is almost a necessity, although having friends with cars is also a bonus. The education level of JCU however, was excellent, and well worth the trip and the stay in Townsville, even though it was a small place with not much city life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I lived in the dorm on campus called Rotary International House, where staff were eager to help out with any issues

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Staff helped me with where to go on the first day of classes, and roommates as well. There was a very detailed orientation for all international students about both studies and life in Townsville

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: None

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Three main dorms, Rotary, Burrulga Yumba and George Roberts. There are also rooms for rent close by campus if you check out facebook groups.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Only george roberts had a meal plan. Otherwise, Rotary had ktichens in each apartment, shared between seven students, while BY had one very large kitchen shared between all 400 students staying

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's a great kickstarter for a social life abroad, and i greatly recommend it. Rotary was like living at a danish collegium. BY is a little more fancy, and newer, which means nicer facilities, like a rooftop terrace, but for me Rotary was perfect, as you got close with you 6 roommates and we had family dinners every other week in our little flat

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: People had very different experiences in Rotary, as it depends highly on your roommates.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: As far as i remember everything went smoothly

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Don't remember but it was not a hustle

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: An email that you could text about questions at any time with quick responses

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was one course i didn't get in the first application round, but after i rent some documentation proving i had the right prerequisits i was accepted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's not difficult. You can also change you subjects up to the day of classes starting, so don't stress about picking the right ones from first try

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Excellent academic programme, highly satisfying and motivating, especially on MB3200 and MB 3190, Marine Conservation and Coral Reef Ecology

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: MB1110 was actually the hardest even though it was a first year course because it was so broad and all about memorising. I more enjoyed the third year classes MB3200 and MB3190 which were challenging but interesting and made a lot of sense

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More including and modern, more encouragement to read first hand litterature and new papers and journals to stay on top of new knowledge which was highly motivating. Much more homework like assignments and articles, but i learned a lot from it - more than i wver had at KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MB1110 - Intruductory Marine Science
MB 2505 - Introduction to GIS
MB3200 - Marine Conservation Biology
MB3190 - Coral Reef Ecology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: MB3200 and MB3190 were excellent and went well together. Morgan Pratchett and Andrew Hoey are at the top of their game at it was a priveledge to undergo their courses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although i didnøt attend i had friends at the ultimate team and the bolley team and they really enjoyed it

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Traditional Thursdays with aunt Vonnie, Volley, Basket, Soccer, Netball, Ultimate fresbee, brunchs, gamenights, trivia nights, etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Try a volley team, and go to uniLodge events, like sip'n'paint and brunch

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Whitsundays, Cairns (Uncle brians tour) Crystal Creek, Alligator Creek, Magnetic Island (i was there 10 times its so good and only a 20 min ferryride from townsville)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy since it was english speaking and very european mixed with some american culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live at a dorm with other aussies

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really, other than the fact that the topic of the first nation people and the colonising history of the country was very sore, and i encourage people who go to australia to seek knowledge and educate themself on the tragic history, to avoid saying something ignorant and offensive, and understand the situation.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The connection with nature, and the politeness and humor

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do weekend trips, get out in the nature, and enjoy it without stressing too much about the homework. Even though it's a lot, you just need to pass, so spend more time exploring than noghts at the library!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the people i met and seeing the wonderfull nature of the country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Financing it

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Stay on top of the process and you wont get stressed. Do it, you won't regret it, and time goes by so fast.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
